{|border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding = "0" width="100%"

|align = "center" bgcolor = "#DDDDDD"|'''Correspondence between SE conversions,&nbsp;''''''bridi&nbsp;''''''place structures, and S'''<sub>'''5'''</sub>

 

|-

|bgcolor = "#DDDDDD"|In Lojban, the&nbsp;cmavo&nbsp;of&nbsp;selma<nowiki>’</nowiki>o&nbsp;SE (<font color="#FF8000">se</font>,&nbsp;<font color="#FF0000">te</font>,&nbsp;<font color="#00FF00">ve</font>, and&nbsp;<font color="#0000FF">xe</font>) used to rearrange the place structures ofbridi&nbsp;happen to correspond to the&nbsp;<font color="#FF0000"><u>permutations</u>&nbsp;</font>(1&nbsp;2), (1&nbsp;3), (1&nbsp;4), and (1&nbsp;5), respectively, on the five main places of a&nbsp;bridi, and together they generate S<sub>5</sub>, the&nbsp;[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_group <font color="#FF0000"><u>symmetric group]</u>&nbsp;</font>on five elements. Thus, using only these four&nbsp;cmavo, one can rearrange a&nbsp;bridi<nowiki>’</nowiki>s five places into any order desired.

 

|-

|bgcolor = "#DDDDDD"|Unfortunately, for mere puny mortals, deriving the needed SEs for a given place structure and interpreting arbitrary SE strings can be tricky & time-consuming. Fortunately, the table below is intended to make this much easier. The first column lists all of the minimum-length SE strings for achieving each place structure, the second column lists the places in the resulting structures, and the third column lists the permutations in S<sub>5</sub>&nbsp;corresponding to each change in place structure. (If you didn<nowiki>’</nowiki>t understand the first paragraph, feel free to ignore the third column.) Note that a place structure may have more than one SE string associated with it, but only the strings of shortest possible length are shown. Thus, if a given SE string does not appear on this page, someone is being more verbose than necessary.

 

|-

|bgcolor = "#DDDDDD"|Note that, if you want to rearrange places beyond x<sub>5</sub>, you<nowiki>’</nowiki>re on your own. Also note that the code for sorting the table doesn<nowiki>’</nowiki>t work entirely well on certain browsers; I am aware of this and am trying to figure out how to fix it.

 

|}
